claim_text: Hackers got unauthorised access to saved-payee data on Wellington IT's platform
summary: Wellington IT, its credit union customers and Ireland's Department of Finance describe an incident in which an outside party exploited a vulnerability in Wellington IT's banking platform and reached saved-payee details.
detail: The Department of Finance statement describes an incident involving payee details, with the vulnerability identified and closed. RTÉ reports Wellington IT said hackers gained unauthorised access; The Record and The Irish Times report the same. The Irish League of Credit Unions called it an IT security incident at a service provider.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: A Tier 1 government statement, plus RTÉ, The Record and The Irish Times as independent outlets.

claim_text: Saved-payee details of credit union app users were exposed
summary: The Department of Finance says it understands the incident involves only payee details for users of credit union mobile banking apps run by Wellington IT; members without the apps are unaffected.
detail: RTÉ explains this means details of the people and businesses members pay, not the members' own account data.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The department's statement, matched by RTÉ and The Irish Times.

claim_text: The payee data may include names, IBANs, addresses and payment references
summary: Wellington IT's disclosures list payee names, bank names, IBANs, BICs, account numbers, sort codes, addresses and payment references. The Register adds saved nicknames and internal reference numbers that do not identify customers.
detail: The lists vary by credit union and by record. Wellington said it cannot yet confirm which individual records were retrieved, so it treats all saved payee records on the platform in the period as potentially affected (Irish Times). Capital and Wexford credit unions say payee addresses were affected only in a limited number of cases, and Wexford says the credit union's name was not visible in the data taken. Limerick & District and Malahide credit unions add that because a saved payee is linked to the member who created it, the data may show a connection between that member and the payee. Ardee Credit Union says the payee's address was potentially affected only in a limited number of instances, and that email addresses and phone numbers were not in the data identified. Claddagh and Enniscorthy credit unions list the same fields: payee name and saved nickname, IBAN, BIC, payee address and payment reference.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Sixteen credit unions' own notices (Tier 1), including North East, Capital, Wexford, Malahide, Phoenix, Member First and North Midlands, list the payee fields; RTÉ, The Register and The Irish Times report the same.
notes: Moved from Reported to Confirmed on Nov 22, 2026 on a credit union's own notice (Tier 1).

claim_text: About 40 to 43 credit unions are affected
summary: Two credit unions' own notices say the affected online banking service is supplied to 43 credit unions. The league's head told RTÉ 43 of 170 were affected.
detail: The Data Protection Commission told The Record it had received more than 40 breach notifications. The league says the breach also reaches credit unions that are not its members. The UK data regulator told The Record it was starting to see reports, so UK members may also be affected. The Irish Examiner reports Wellington IT serves 50 credit unions, 43 of them in Ireland; North East Credit Union says almost 50 other credit unions use Wellington. The Irish Examiner also reports Wellington supports 43 of Ireland's largest credit unions, with a 51% share of the Irish market. St. Canice's Credit Union says the wider incident is understood to affect approximately 50 credit unions. Phoenix Credit Union's notice also says approximately 50 credit unions use the same supplier's service.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Two credit unions' own notices (Tier 1) give the 43 figure; the league's chief (RTÉ) and the data regulator's count (The Record) agree independently.
notes: Moved from Reported to Confirmed on Nov 22, 2026 on two credit unions' own notices (Tier 1).

claim_text: How many members are affected
summary: No exact number of affected users has been published. RTÉ and The Irish Times say potentially hundreds of thousands; the Department of Finance says finding the exact figure is a key priority of the outside review.
detail: 'Hundreds of thousands' is an outlet estimate, not an official figure. The Irish Examiner says Wellington currently supports 1.8 million credit union members overall; that is its customer base, not a count of people affected.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: The department says the exact number is still unknown.

claim_text: Wellington IT told credit unions about 1.4 million malicious requests
summary: Wellington IT told credit unions on Nov 16 that a 'bad actor' made some 1.4 million malicious requests and retrieved saved payee records (The Irish Times). The league's chief put the activity at Oct 2 to 4.
detail: The Irish Times says the weakness was exploited on Oct 6, but Capital and Wexford credit unions' own notices, relaying Wellington, say it was exploited Oct 2 to 4 and closed Oct 6, matching the league and The Register. We use Oct 2 to 4 for the activity and Oct 6 for the fix. The Irish Examiner, which saw Wellington's Nov 16 correspondence, gives about five million requests instead (c017); the two figures have not been reconciled.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Wellington's email and the league's account, relayed by three outlets, all from Wellington's information.

claim_text: Wellington IT says the vulnerability is closed
summary: The Department of Finance says it is informed by Wellington IT that the vulnerability has been identified and closed. The league says it understands it was closed on Oct 6.
detail: The Irish Times reports Wellington told credit unions it had closed the vulnerability. Capital and Wexford credit unions' notices say Wellington told them it was closed on Oct 6. Ardee Credit Union's notice gives the same dates: exploited Oct 2 to 4, closed Oct 6. CANA, St. Canice's, First South, Phoenix and Tullamore credit unions say the vulnerability has been closed or fixed. Lisduggan, Claddagh and Enniscorthy credit unions say the relevant vulnerability has been closed.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The department's statement, matched by two independent outlets.

claim_text: Wellington IT spotted a possible breach on Nov 15, six weeks after the activity
summary: The league's chief told RTÉ that Wellington IT's early investigation did not identify a data protection breach, that it detected a possible breach on Nov 15, and that it told credit unions on Nov 16.
detail: The Record reports the same account, attributing it to the league's chief speaking to RTÉ. Wellington's chief executive said the company alerted customers 'as soon as we confirmed the potential risk to customer data.' Separately, the Irish Examiner reports Wellington's own correspondence said its initial investigation into the October activity found 'no exposure', and that on the Sunday morning its engineers concluded saved payee data may have been retrieved.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The league's account (RTÉ, relayed by The Record) and Wellington's own correspondence as reported by the Irish Examiner give the same sequence.
notes: Moved from Reported to Confirmed on Nov 22, 2026: a second independent account (Irish Examiner).

claim_text: The Department of Finance first learned of it on Nov 17
summary: The Department of Finance says it first became aware of the incident on Nov 17 and has been engaging closely with those involved.
detail: A junior finance minister convened a meeting with Wellington IT and the credit union sector on Nov 19.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The department's own statement.

claim_text: A junior finance minister called the delay in telling credit unions 'not acceptable'
summary: A junior finance minister, responsible for credit unions, said many credit unions were only told of the breach in recent days although it happened in October, and described the delay by the supplier as 'not acceptable'.
detail: The Record quotes the same official using the words 'simply not acceptable.'
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: An on-the-record statement, reported by three independent outlets.

claim_text: Whether any money was taken
summary: Ireland's Department of Finance says there is no evidence at present that members' funds were accessed or that fraud occurred. The national cyber centre (per The Record) and the league say the same.
detail: These are 'no evidence yet' statements from early in the investigation, not a finding that no money was taken. Health Services Staffs Credit Union tells members their money is safe and there is no evidence accounts or balances were compromised. Ardee Credit Union says that, given the limited payee data involved, it does not see a high risk of fraud or phishing; St. Canice's tells members their money is safe.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: Officials say no evidence so far; the review is not finished.

claim_text: Passwords, PINs, logins and balances were not accessed, per Wellington and the credit unions
summary: Wellington IT told credit unions that members' account details, passwords, PINs and balances were not accessed, according to The Irish Times. The league says it has seen no issue with members' banking credentials.
detail: Individual credit unions told members their login details and PINs were unaffected (The Register). North East Credit Union's notice says Wellington IT confirmed members' account numbers, balances, transaction details and login details were not involved. Capital Credit Union's notice says the provider confirmed member accounts, balances, the number of transactions and amounts were not accessed. Wexford Credit Union's notice says member account details, balances and online banking logins were not accessed, and adds members' email addresses and phone numbers. Limerick & District and Malahide credit unions say their core banking systems were not accessed, and that balances, transaction histories, passwords and PINs were not compromised. Ardee, St. Canice's and First South credit unions say online banking passwords, PINs and login credentials were not affected; Ardee says login credentials are not stored on the platform. Phoenix Credit Union says passwords, PINs, payment card details and login credentials were not compromised; Tullamore says member accounts and balances were not compromised. Lisduggan, Claddagh and Enniscorthy credit unions say member accounts and balances have not been compromised.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Five credit unions' own notices (Tier 1) state what Wellington confirmed to them; the league and outlets report the same. This confirms what Wellington told them; the outside review is not finished.
notes: Moved from Reported to Confirmed on Nov 22, 2026 on credit unions' own notices (Tier 1).

claim_text: Who is behind the attack
summary: Wellington IT and officials call the attacker a 'bad actor'. No attacker is named and no claim of responsibility appears in the sources we read.
detail: This page does not name or guess at an attacker. Extortion emails were sent to Wellington IT and several credit unions (c019), but no source says who sent them.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: Nothing public names the attacker.

claim_text: How the vulnerability worked
summary: Wellington IT has not published technical detail. Per the Irish Examiner, its letter calls it an 'authorisation flaw' used by a script with a valid member login (c017); how the login was obtained is not public.
detail: Wellington has engaged outside cybersecurity experts to review the incident.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: Only a one-line description, relayed by one outlet; no technical detail has been published.

claim_text: Irish regulators, police and the national cyber centre are involved
summary: The Department of Finance says Wellington IT committed to keep engaging the National Cyber Security Centre, the national police, the Data Protection Commission and the Central Bank of Ireland.
detail: The Data Protection Commission told RTÉ it is assessing the notifications as a matter of priority. The Irish Examiner reports the finance minister told government TDs and senators the circumstances needed to be established, with the department briefed by the Central Bank and the Data Protection Commission investigating. The Irish Times reports a Central Bank deputy governor said the bank is 'fully engaged' with the affected credit unions.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The department's statement, matched by RTÉ and The Record.

claim_text: Wellington IT hired outside experts; the department asked for the review's terms
summary: The Department of Finance says Wellington IT engaged external cybersecurity experts for a comprehensive review, including the exact number of accounts and users affected, and that the minister asked for the review's terms of reference.
detail: The department says no conclusions should be drawn until the review is complete.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The department's statement; The Register reports the same hiring.

claim_text: Wellington IT says an automated script with a valid member login exploited an 'authorisation flaw'
summary: Wellington IT's Nov 16 letter to credit unions, seen by the Irish Examiner, says an automated client with a valid member login made about five million requests on Oct 2 to 4 to exploit an 'authorisation flaw'.
detail: BleepingComputer repeats the Irish Examiner's account. The league's chief gave RTÉ a figure of 1.4 million (c006).
label: Reported
why_it_supports: One outlet's reading of Wellington's correspondence; BleepingComputer relays the same report, so it counts once.

claim_text: Wellington IT cannot tell which payee records were taken, so treats all as potentially affected
summary: Wellington IT's letter, quoted by the Irish Examiner, says logs showing which members were requested are not available, so it treats all saved payee records from that period as potentially affected.
detail: The Irish Times reports the same: Wellington cannot yet confirm which individual records were retrieved. Capital and Wexford credit unions' notices say the investigation could not tell whether all or some saved payee information was retrieved, so the provider treats all saved payees for their members as potentially affected. The notices do not mention logs.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Two credit unions' own notices (Tier 1) state it; the Irish Examiner and The Irish Times report the same from Wellington's correspondence. The missing-logs reason rests on the Irish Examiner alone.
notes: Moved from Reported to Confirmed on Nov 22, 2026 on credit unions' own notices (Tier 1); claim wording narrowed to what the notices say.

claim_text: Extortion emails were sent to Wellington IT and several credit unions
summary: Wellington IT's letter, per the Irish Examiner, says a credit union told it extortion emails had been sent to Wellington and several credit unions; they had gone to junk mail unseen.
detail: No source we read says who sent the emails, what they asked for, or whether they came from the attacker.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: One outlet's reading of Wellington's correspondence.

claim_text: Credit union bodies called for clarity on how many members are affected
summary: After the Nov 19 meeting, the Irish League of Credit Unions and two other sector bodies issued a joint statement calling for the exact number of affected accounts and users to be found quickly.
detail: The bodies urged members never to share a PIN, password or one-time passcode, even with someone claiming to be from their credit union.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: One outlet reporting the joint statement; the statement itself was not read.

claim_text: The Central Bank urged credit union members to be extra wary of scam calls and texts
summary: The Irish Times reports that senior Central Bank of Ireland officials told members of affected credit unions, and people who receive payments from them, to be wary of texts, calls and emails asking for financial details.
detail: A deputy governor said it is most unusual for a bank or provider to ask for those specific details. The Department of Finance and the credit unions' notices give the same advice to stay alert to phishing and impersonation.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: One Tier 2 report of the Central Bank's remarks at a press briefing; no Central Bank statement on this incident was found on its own site.
